interest: 1944 State Department planning for a Japanese leadership flight to the mainland.
overview: Two July 1944 memoranda on the risk that Japan's Emperor and leaders might flee to China or Manchuria; Ballantine proposes treating flight as abdication.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Adviser on Political Relations, Department of State

people.name: Joseph W. Ballantine
people.role: Deputy Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Recommendations by Far Eastern Affairs officer J. W. Ballantine for amending a memorandum to Assistant Secretary Long concerning continental Japanese resistance and the propaganda use of an imperial abdication.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (Office of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Ballantine proposes that any continental regime would depend on Manchuria, and that a fleeing Emperor could be declared to have abdicated.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from J. W. Ballantine to Joseph C. Grew regarding Continental Regime and Emperor's Abdication
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew (Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Inquiry by Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long on whether State Department planning has addressed the potential flight of the Japanese Royal Family, High Command, and civilian leadership to China.
subfiles.summary: Breckinridge Long warns Grew that Japan's Emperor and leaders might flee to China for prolonged resistance and asks for plans to counter this.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Assistant Secretary Breckinridge Long to Joseph C. Grew regarding Possible Japanese Flight to China
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew (Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs)
